title: The mound holes are partly the colony's road to the food
question: The fix that stops mound digging (bottom) also seals the hollow mound the ants walk through to reach the food, and the colony shrinks by a third to a half. Is the hollow, ant-filled mound (top) acceptable as their passage? Or do you want a solid mound, with the ants given another way to the food (a trail over it, or a second door on the food's side)?
context_md: Follow-up to the mound-diggers trace (PR 664). I built your three levers as one switch (MOUND_DIG) and measured them on steady food with your switches. Every lever that stops the digging costs the colony: mean 268-275 ants -> 134-198 with all three on, and 101-178 ants a run starve trapped inside the mound against 2-43. The part that only stops the dig-down turn changes nothing either way. So the switch ships off, recorded as a dead end until a rule can tell a passage from a pointless scrape.
